# Data

------------------------------------------------------------------------

```{r}
# samples metadata
sp <- read_csv(file.path(cfg$project$data,"imagery_zooscan_samples+acquisitions_cleaned.csv")) %>% 
  distinct(acquisid,sampleid,genid,d,latitude)

# community grey
grey <- read_csv(file.path(cfg$project$data,
                           "imagery_zooscan_objects_morpho_taxo_cleaned.csv")) %>% 
  left_join(sp) %>% 
  group_by(genid) %>%
  summarize(gmedian=sum(grey_median*d)/sum(d))

# samples abundances
abundance_class <- read_csv(file.path(cfg$project$data,
                           "imagery_zooscan_objects_morpho_taxo_cleaned.csv")) %>%
  left_join(sp) %>% 
  group_by(genid,class_phylum_detailed_copepods) %>% 
  summarize(count=sum(d))

abundance_family <- read_csv(file.path(cfg$project$data,
                           "imagery_zooscan_objects_morpho_taxo_cleaned.csv")) %>%
  left_join(sp) %>% 
  group_by(genid,order_class) %>% 
  summarize(count=sum(d))

# environmental data
envt <- read_csv(file.path(cfg$project$data,"environment_CMEMS_model+satellite.csv")) %>% 
  select(genid,nppv,si,po4,no3,o2,KD490,ZSD,sst,chl) %>% 
  distinct() 
```

## Class/Phylum

We only consider classes with more than 10#/L within the whole dataset and present in at least 5 samples.

```{r}
abundance_class %>% group_by(class_phylum_detailed_copepods) %>%
  summarize(count=sum(count)) %>%
  arrange()

abundance_class %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  count(class_phylum_detailed_copepods) %>% 
  arrange(n)

# remove groups with less than 10 #/L over the whole dataset 
abundance_class <- abundance_class %>%
  ungroup() %>% 
  group_by(class_phylum_detailed_copepods) %>%
  filter(n() > 5 & sum(count) > 10) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from="class_phylum_detailed_copepods",values_from="count",values_fill=0) 
```

Hellinger transformation:

```{r}
# Hellinger transformation for abundances
data.h <- decostand(abundance_class[,2:ncol(abundance_class)],method="hellinger")
data_class <- bind_cols(genid=abundance_class$genid,data.h) 
```

Let's make the dataset for the Ridge:

```{r}
grey_envt_ab_class <- left_join(envt,grey) %>% 
  left_join(data_class) %>% 
  # remove samples with NA values (i.e. 13 samples)
  drop_na() %>% 
  # remove one outlier in Si (x3 the highest other values), otherwise it will drive the scaling
  filter(si < 300) %>% 
  # need to be on the same scale for comparison -> handled by cv.glmnet but easier to do it for plotting comparison of effects
  mutate(across(-c(gmedian, genid), ~ (.-min(.)) / (max(.) - min(.)))) 
```

Ridge model:

```{r}
set.seed(123)

# Exclude 'sampleid' and 'gmedian' columns
X <- as.matrix(grey_envt_ab_class %>% select(-gmedian, -genid))

# Response variable
y <- grey_envt_ab_class$gmedian

# Fit Ridge regression model with cross-validation to find optimal lambda
ridge_model <- cv.glmnet(X, y, alpha = 0)

# Plot cross-validation results to visualize the optimal lambda
# plot(ridge_model)

y_pred <- predict(ridge_model, newx = X, s = "lambda.min")
r_squared <- 1 - sum((y - y_pred)^2) / sum((y - mean(y))^2)
r_squared

# Extract coefficients for the optimal lambda
coef_ridge <- coef(ridge_model, s = "lambda.min")
coef_tibble <- as_tibble(as.matrix(coef_ridge), rownames = "variable") %>%
  rename(coefficient = `lambda.min`) %>%
  filter(variable != "(Intercept)")  # Optionally exclude the intercept
  
# Plot coefficients with ggplot
ridge_class <- ggplot(coef_tibble, aes(x = reorder(variable, coefficient), y = coefficient, color = coefficient)) +                              # Add points
  geom_segment(aes(x = variable, xend = variable, y = 0, yend = coefficient),  # Add line to 0
               color = "gray50") +
  geom_point(size = 4) + 
  scale_color_gradient2(low = "blue", mid = "white", high = "red", midpoint = 0) +  # Color scale
  coord_flip() +                                    # Flip coordinates for better readability
  labs(title = "", 
       x = "", 
       y = "Ridge coefficient value") +
  theme_minimal() + 
  theme(legend.position="none",
        text=element_text(size=12))
ridge_class
```

## Order

```{r}
abundance_family %>% group_by(order_class) %>%

# remove groups with less than 10 #/L over the whole dataset and 5 samples

```

Hellinger transformation:

```{r}

```

Let's make the dataset for the Ridge:

```{r}
grey_envt_ab_family <- left_join(envt,grey) %>%

  drop_na() %>% 
  mutate(across(-c(gmedian, genid), ~ (.-min(.)) / (max(.) - min(.)))) 
```

Ridge model:

```{r}
set.seed(123)

# Exclude 'sampleid' and 'gmedian' columns
X <- as.matrix(grey_envt_ab_family %>% select(-gmedian, -genid))

# Response variable
y <- grey_envt_ab_family$gmedian

# Fit Ridge regression model with cross-validation to find optimal lambda
ridge_model <- cv.glmnet(X, y, alpha = 0)

# Plot cross-validation results to visualize the optimal lambda
# plot(ridge_model)

y_pred <- predict(ridge_model, newx = X, s = "lambda.min")
r_squared <- 1 - sum((y - y_pred)^2) / sum((y - mean(y))^2)
r_squared

# Extract coefficients for the optimal lambda
coef_ridge <- coef(ridge_model, s = "lambda.min")
coef_tibble <- as_tibble(as.matrix(coef_ridge), rownames = "variable") %>%
  rename(coefficient = `lambda.min`) %>%
  filter(variable != "(Intercept)")  # Optionally exclude the intercept
  
# Plot coefficients with ggplot
ridge_family <- ggplot(coef_tibble, aes(x = reorder(variable, coefficient), y = coefficient, color = coefficient)) +                              # Add points
  geom_segment(aes(x = variable, xend = variable, y = 0, yend = coefficient),  # Add line to 0
               color = "gray50") +
  geom_point(size = 4) + 
  scale_color_gradient2(low = "blue", mid = "white", high = "red", midpoint = 0) +  # Color scale
  coord_flip() +                                    # Flip coordinates for better readability
  labs(title = "", 
       x = "", 
       y = "Ridge coefficient value") +
  theme_minimal() + 
  theme(legend.position="none",
        text=element_text(size=12))
ridge_family
```

# Summary graph

```{r}
spobj_mean_envt <- left_join(envt,distinct(sp,genid,latitude)) %>% 
  left_join(grey)
```

```{r}
both_binned <- read_csv(file.path(cfg$project$data,
                           "imagery_zooscan_objects_morpho_taxo_cleaned.csv")) %>%
  left_join(sp) %>% 
  group_by(genid,latitude) %>% 
  summarize(gmedian=sum(d*grey_median)/sum(d)) %>% 
  right_join(envt) %>% 
  drop_na() %>% 
  mutate(latitude=abs(latitude)) %>% 
  # Bin euphotic depth into 2500 intervals and latitude into 20 intervals
  mutate(
    zsd_bin = cut(ZSD, breaks = seq(0,80, by = 15), include.lowest = TRUE, right = FALSE),
    lat_bin = cut(abs(latitude), breaks = seq(0,90, by = 15), include.lowest = TRUE, right = FALSE)
  ) %>%
  # Calculate the midpoint of each bin for both concentration and latitude
  mutate(
    zsd_mid = as.numeric(str_split_i(gsub("\\[|\\)", "", zsd_bin),",",1)),
    lat_mid = as.numeric(str_split_i(gsub("\\[|\\)", "", lat_bin),",",1))
  ) %>%
  # Summarize gmedian by averaging within each bin
  group_by(zsd_mid, lat_mid) %>%
  summarize(
    avg_gmedian = mean(gmedian, na.rm = TRUE),
    n=n(),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) 
```

```{r}
fitted_surface <- surf.ls(2, both_binned$lat_mid, both_binned$zsd_mid, 
                          both_binned$avg_gmedian)
# compute the values at given points on a grid
values_on_grid <- trmat(fitted_surface, min(both_binned$lat_mid), max(both_binned$lat_mid), min(both_binned$zsd_mid), max(both_binned$zsd_mid), 50)

# plot the grid while superposing the points
interp_plot <- ggplot() +
  geom_raster(aes(x=x, y=y, fill=z), data=broom::tidy(values_on_grid)) +
  geom_point( aes(x=lat_mid, y=zsd_mid, fill=avg_gmedian, size=n), shape=21, data=both_binned) +
  #scale_fill_gradient(low = "black", high = "white") + 
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option="A") + 
  theme_classic() + 
  #scale_y_reverse() + 
  labs(x="Latitude",y="Euphotic depth (m)",
       size="Number \nof samples",
       fill="Average \nmedian grey") + 
  theme(text=element_text(size=12))
interp_plot
```

```{r}
bot <- ridge_class + interp_plot + plot_layout(ncol=2,widths=c(1,1.25)) + 
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = list(c("b","c"))) &  # manual tag list
  theme(plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.tag.position = "topleft")
bot
```
